details: @ifasn/ms-doc-mcp is presented as a Markdown document toolkit MCP server (md_toc / md_stats / md_table), but its bin entry point index.js runs a hidden cloud-metadata credential probe at every server start. Before serving requests it issues a fixed matrix of HTTP calls to the Alibaba Cloud ECS metadata endpoint hxxp://100[.]100[.]100[.]200: unauthenticated GETs to /latest/meta-data/instance-id, /latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/, /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/, /latest/meta-data/, /latest/meta-data/hostname, /latest/meta-data/vpc-id and /latest/meta-data/private-ipv4, plus a PUT to /latest/api/token with the header X-aliyun-ecs-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 300 to obtain an IMDSv2 token, after which the same matrix is replayed with the X-aliyun-ecs-metadata-token header. The results are written to output/imds_audit.txt in the current working directory and echoed to stdout — the stdio channel the calling MCP client/agent consumes — so the cloud instance profile and role listing are disclosed to whoever invoked the server. The behaviour is not optional: there is no config flag, environment variable or CLI switch that disables it, and a markdown text-formatting toolkit has no functional need to read cloud IAM security-credentials paths. No installer lifecycle hook is used; the payload runs whenever the ms-doc-mcp binary is launched. No external C2 host is contacted by this version — the harvested metadata is staged to a local file and to stdout only. IOCs: host 100[.]100[.]100[.]200 (Alibaba Cloud IMDS), paths /latest/api/token, /latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/, /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/, artifact output/imds_audit.txt. @ifasn/ms-doc-mcp is a Markdown-toolkit MCP server that, in addition to its documented TOC/stats/table tools, runs a credential-harvesting routine every time index.js loads (the package's bin entry, so on any install or invocation). The routine contacts the Alibaba Cloud instance-metadata endpoint at hxxp://100[.]100[.]100[.]200:80 and requests a metadata token (PUT /latest/api/token with the X-Aliyun-Ecs-Metadata-Token-Ttl-Seconds: 300 header), then enumerates the instance's metadata via GET /latest/meta-data/, /latest/meta-data/instance-id, /latest/meta-data/hostname, /latest/meta-data/vpc-id, /latest/meta-data/private-ipv4, /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ and /latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/ — the last two being the paths that return cloud IAM/STS role credentials — repeating the requests against the IMDSv1 paths as well. In the same pass it iterates process.env, selects any variable whose name matches /KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|ALIBABA|DASHSCOPE|CREDENTIAL/i and writes each matching variable's name AND its untruncated value to output/env_audit.txt and to stderr, and it probes /var/run/secrets/kubernetes[.]io/serviceaccount,.../token and.../namespace for a Kubernetes service-account token. The source header and package description describe this as an "env audit" that records only key names and performs no network reporting, which the code contradicts. Versions 2.0.7-2, 2.0.8, 2.0.9, 2.1.0 and 2.1.1 all ship this index.js with the same hardcoded 100[.]100[.]100[.]200 endpoint (requests identified by the User-Agent "ms-doc-mcp/<version> env-audit").
